1.why: authorized() derives the account solely from the server-side session's userId and every MFA endpoint uses it, so a user can only ever reach their own MFA settings (no client-supplied identifiers).

2.why: Each code is stored as a hash on the requesting session and compared only against that session's own challenge, so codes are not valid across users — only the demo-mode fixed value 123456 is shared.

3.why: Nothing invalidates sessions when MFA is enabled (sessions.delete is only called on sign-in rotation, logout, or timeout), so any pre-existing sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted (session.pendingSecret then account.secret) and recovery codes are kept only as peppered SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: Secrets, identity codes, and recovery codes are generated with randomBytes/randomInt from Node's crypto module, i.e., a CSPRNG.

6.why: The client keeps the CSRF token, setup key, and codes only in in-memory variables with no localStorage/sessionStorage use, and the session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

7.why: Email, delivery method, OTP, and recovery-code inputs are all validated server-side via emailOK/otpOK/codeOK regexes, allow-lists, and a 10 kB body cap.

8.why: All dynamic values are rendered with textContent (never innerHTML) and responses carry a nonce-based CSP, so injected markup or script cannot execute.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all — navigation is internal SPA view switching — so no open redirect can exist.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and more on every response including errors.

11.why: cookieValue() sets the mfa_session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Server logs and error output contain no secrets or stack traces, but the seed is embedded in the otpauth:// URI query string and demo mode returns codes that the client writes to the browser console.

13.why: Identity challenges carry a used flag and a 10-minute expiry (checked before acceptance), and recovery codes are marked used on redemption and rejected thereafter.

14.why: failed() locks each per-account failure counter for 15 minutes after 5 attempts on every verification endpoint, and code requests are capped at 3 per 15 minutes.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID (rotation), getSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
